name: MediaForge
description: Compresses images and videos during upload, before they are committed to the file store.

settings_schema.header:
Files are shrunk while they are uploaded, so the small version is what reaches the server. Changes apply to the next upload; no restart needed.

An invalid value is ignored, the standard value is used, and a warning naming the setting goes to the server log.
settings_schema.footer:
Files that are already small, formats that cannot be read, and anything that fails are stored exactly as sent — compression never makes an upload fail.

[Open the MediaForge report](/plugins/com.github.berzionline.mediaforge/report) for what was saved, by day and by type. Administrators only.

settings.help_text: Whether ffmpeg is present and what the plugin can currently do. Without ffmpeg, images still work; video and voice messages do not.

sections.title: Images
sections.subtitle: Photos and screenshots, shrunk as they are uploaded

settings.help_text: Shrinks JPEG and PNG images as they are uploaded. Off means every image is stored exactly as sent.
Images larger than this are scaled down; the aspect ratio is kept. 1920 suits normal viewing. Allowed: 100–10000.
Higher means better quality and larger files. 82 is close to indistinguishable from the original. Allowed: 1–100.
Files below this are stored unchanged. Compressing a small image often makes it bigger. Allowed: 0–100000.

options.display_name: Keep — camera details, date and location stay in the file
Remove — strip all hidden information, including location

settings.help_text: Photos carry the camera, the date and often the location they were taken (GPS). Removing it is smaller and better for privacy; keeping it preserves orientation and copyright.

settings.display_name: Compress this many images at the same time
settings.help_text: How many images compress at once. Each one needs memory for the full picture, so 4 is recommended. Above the limit, images are stored as sent rather than queued. Allowed: 1–256.

Converts videos as they are uploaded, so the smaller version is what reaches the server. Needs ffmpeg installed. If a conversion fails, the upload is refused rather than stored unconverted. Off means every video is stored exactly as sent.
Taller videos are scaled down to this height; the aspect ratio is kept. 1080 is full HD and suits normal viewing. Allowed: 240–4320.

options.display_name: H.264 in MP4 — plays on every device (recommended)
H.265 in MP4 — about 30% smaller, but not every device plays it
AV1 in WebM — the smallest files, but only recent devices play them

settings.help_text:
**H.264** plays everywhere: iPhone, Android, Windows, Safari, Chrome, Firefox. Choose it unless you have a reason not to.

**H.265** is about a third smaller, but does not play in Firefox, in Chrome on most machines, or on Android before ~2017. Needs the HEVC extension on Windows.

**AV1** is smallest, but does not play on iPhone before iOS 17 or on most smart TVs, and converts much more slowly.

Stored videos keep the format they were saved in — test before switching.
Picture quality of the converted video. Lower means better quality and larger files, higher means smaller and softer. 23 is a good balance. Allowed: 0–51.
Sound quality of the converted video. 128 is fine for speech and music; below 64 speech starts to sound thin. Allowed: 8–512.

A conversion running longer than this is abandoned and the video is stored exactly as sent. Keep it below the server's own write timeout, or the upload breaks before this takes effect. Allowed: 10–86400.

settings.display_name: Do not convert videos larger than (MB)
settings.help_text: Videos above this size are stored as sent without being converted, because very large files take disproportionately long. Allowed: 1–100000.

settings.display_name: Convert this many videos at the same time
settings.help_text: How many videos convert at once. One video already uses every processor core, so a higher value makes the server slow for everyone without finishing sooner; 1 is recommended. Above the limit, videos are stored as sent. Allowed: 1–64.

settings.display_name: Mark compressed files in their filename
settings.help_text: Adds a marker to the filename of files that were made smaller, so the original and the compressed copy are told apart on download.

sections.title: Voice messages
sections.subtitle: Recording and converting speech — needs ffmpeg

settings.help_text: Adds a microphone button for recording voice messages. Needs ffmpeg. Recordings are stored as ordinary audio attachments.
Longer recordings are refused before anything is stored, measured on what was spoken. Allowed: 5–3600.

settings.display_name: Shorten long pauses in voice messages
settings.help_text: Shortens the silent gaps inside a recording. This removes part of what was said and cannot be undone, which is why it is off by default. Pauses are shortened rather than deleted, and the start is never trimmed.
Empty means everywhere. Otherwise list channels by URL name, display name or ID, separated by commas. Elsewhere the microphone is hidden.
